problem: Understanding the relationship between Bayesian posterior sampling and stochastic gradient descent training dynamics in neural networks remains unresolved in deep learning theory.
approach: Model SGD's long-term behavior as diffusion on porous media using singular learning theory, analyzing how loss surface degeneracies shape the late-stage steady-state distribution.
contribution: Shows that SGD's local steady-state distribution is a tempered version of the Bayesian posterior when hyperparameters are chosen appropriately.

problem: Existing diffusion models treat quantized data (e.g., 8-bit pixels) as continuous or add noise to approximate continuity, neither guaranteeing that samples converge to the true discrete value set.
approach: Explicitly parameterize diffusion models to account for quantization, ensuring the reverse process converges to quantized points with a specific parameterization strategy.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art likelihood on CIFAR-10 image generation, improving negative log-likelihood from 2.42 to 0.27 while approaching the theoretical lower bound.

problem: LLMs frequently hallucinate, generating inconsistent content; existing mitigation methods (RAG, RLHF) are resource-intensive while decoding-based methods lack explicit hallucination control.
approach: Perform token-level internal verification at each reasoning step using self-checking decoding, evaluate candidate fragments in latent space with explicit hallucination risk scoring, and iteratively prune/regenerate errors.
contribution: Reduces hallucinations and improves generation accuracy on HALU datasets with a scalable, lightweight decoding-based solution.

problem: Causal effect estimation under unmeasured confounding via front-door adjustment has focused on average treatment effects; heterogeneous effect estimation remains underexplored.
approach: Develop two debiased learners (FD-DR-Learner and FD-R-Learner) for heterogeneous front-door effects with quasi-oracle convergence rates even when nuisance functions converge slowly.
contribution: Achieve fast convergence and debiased heterogeneous treatment effect estimates under the front-door scenario with quasi-oracle rate guarantees.

problem: Existing video relighting diffusion models lack explicit control over illumination changes despite achieving good visual results.
approach: Combine pre-trained image relighting and video diffusion priors in a training-free manner with light trajectory injection into latent space and geometry-aware frequency-domain latent blending.
contribution: First controllable video relighting method enabling explicit illumination control via user-supplied light trajectories without retraining.

problem: Identifying optimal data mixture for pre-training and post-training large models is a significant bottleneck requiring expensive search or heuristics.
approach: Reformulate mixture selection as bilevel optimization showing equivalence between optimizing mixture ratios and per-source loss weighting; implement gradient-based alternating optimization of model and mixture.
contribution: FastMix achieves average score 48.2 in pre-training with only 1.3 GPU-hours (550× faster than RegMix, 55× faster than CLIMB) and leads post-training SFT with +5.5 gain.

problem: Visual language models incur excessive computational overhead when processing long videos due to high frame rates and durations, limiting deployment in resource-constrained environments.
approach: Use reinforcement learning with structured memory retrieval to select query-relevant clips and compress tokens, applying compression-aware GRPO to distill from teacher to student network.
contribution: MARC achieves efficient video understanding through RL-based token compression with memory-augmented retrieval while preserving reasoning ability.

problem: Standard RL analyses assume finite-dimensional function spaces; applying PPO and TD methods in infinite-dimensional spaces without clear theoretical guarantees remains unaddressed.
approach: Analyze PPO through a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) perspective, using kernelized TD critic for efficient policy evaluation and KL-regularized natural gradient for policy improvement.
contribution: Provide non-asymptotic instance-adaptive convergence rates with optimal k^(-1/2) complexity for stochastic optimization, unifying tabular through neural tangent kernel regimes.

problem: Spiking neural networks remain biologically underutilized due to oversimplified neuron models (e.g., leaky integrate-and-fire) that omit dynamic conductance mechanisms, limiting noise robustness.
approach: Introduce Dynamic Gated Neuron (DGN) where membrane conductance evolves in response to activity, enabling selective input filtering and adaptive noise suppression as a bio-inspired gating mechanism.
contribution: Establish dynamic gating as key to robust spike-based computation with enhanced stochastic stability and superior performance on anti-noise and temporal tasks like TIDIGITS and SHD.

problem: Weak-to-strong generalization via pseudolabel fine-tuning breaks when pseudolabel distribution differs from labeled distribution due to group imbalance in spurious correlation settings.
approach: Characterize W2S gain at proportional asymptotic limit and propose group-label-free retraining on high-confidence data subsets after W2S fine-tuning.
contribution: Show W2S gain diminishes as squared imbalance increases; algorithm recovers performance without access to group labels with consistent improvements over vanilla W2S.

problem: Flow-based super-resolution models require many denoising steps for quality, or rely on model distillation that locks in fixed fidelity-realism trade-offs.
approach: Train flow-based teacher super-resolution model, then distill by aligning one-step student predictions to the teacher's ODE trajectory at intermediate states.
contribution: OFTSR achieves state-of-the-art one-step image super-resolution on FFHQ/DIV2K/ImageNet with tunable fidelity-realism trade-off.

problem: Watermarking diffusion models requires either post-hoc schemes or model modification, with limited robustness to unseen attacks.
approach: Embed watermarks during the diffusion process by guiding with gradients from off-the-shelf decoders and image augmentations, increasing robustness without retraining.
contribution: Guidance-based watermarking converts post-hoc schemes into in-process embedding, complementary to VAE-level watermarking while preserving image diversity and quality.

problem: Applying RL to reachability problems faces a mismatch: standard RL optimizes expected returns while reachability needs to maximize safe states indefinitely, especially on low-probability regions.
approach: Propose Feasibility-Guided Exploration that identifies feasible initial conditions and learns safe policies via robust optimization over discovered feasible subsets.
contribution: FGE learns policies with over 50% more coverage on challenging initial conditions across MuJoCo and Kinetix tasks compared to prior methods.

problem: Time series foundation models' behavior is strongly shaped by subtle design choices (patch size, embedding, training objective), yet these implicit biases remain poorly understood.
approach: Mix theory and controlled empirical evaluation to identify how design choices induce implicit biases in fundamental properties like temporal behavior and mean-reversion.
contribution: Characterize how various design knobs affect TSFM quality and show these biases interact in complex ways, illustrated through outlier handling case study.

problem: Multi-user contextual bandits with graph-structured users and non-linear reward functions lack principled methods that exploit both graph structure and function smoothness.
approach: Unify graph-regularized reward functions into a single multi-user RKHS with explicit graph-Laplacian kernel fusion, enabling GP-based algorithms LK-GP-UCB and LK-GP-TS.
contribution: Provide regret bounds scaling with effective dimension of multi-user kernel rather than user count or ambient dimension, outperforming non-graph-aware baselines.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning has proven effective in text LLMs but extending to multimodal settings requires modeling visual state transitions alongside textual reasoning, challenging existing approaches.
approach: Introduce Uni-CoT with macro-level planning CoT and micro-level subtask CoT to capture visual transitions aligned with textual logic, using structured training with auxiliary tasks.
contribution: Achieve state-of-the-art performance on reasoning-driven image generation and understanding with remarkable generalization.

problem: Expressive speech-to-speech translation requires preserving speaker identity and emotional style while handling scarcity of paired expressive data and complex multi-stage pipelines.
approach: Build unified single-stage framework with speech semantic and style modeling integrated with text-based LLM, using cross-modal chain-of-thought prompting for style preservation.
contribution: UniSS with 44.8k hours of UniST dataset significantly outperforms prior methods while preserving voice, emotion, and duration consistency.

problem: Ultra-high-resolution image synthesis remains computationally expensive and struggles to preserve fine-grained visual details and textures.
approach: Introduce Latent Wavelet Diffusion with frequency-aware masking from wavelet energy maps to dynamically focus training on detail-rich regions and scale-consistent VAE objective.
contribution: LWD improves perceptual quality and FID scores on 2K-4K synthesis without architectural changes or inference overhead.

problem: Existing protein structure tokenizers require complex SE(3)-invariant operations and bespoke components that are hard to optimize and scale.
approach: Present Kanzi, a flow-based tokenizer using diffusion autoencoder with flow matching loss, replacing frame-based representations with global coordinates and standard attention.
contribution: Kanzi outperforms existing tokenizers on reconstruction with smaller model size and lower training cost; autoregressive generation outperforms token-based models.

problem: Incorporating symmetries into generative models improves training but existing methods cannot learn broken symmetries that arise in complex systems.
approach: Introduce Symmetry-Enforcing Stochastic Modulation (SESaMo) enabling normalized flows to enforce exact symmetries while learning broken symmetries through stochastic modulation.
contribution: Benchmark SESaMo on mixture models and field theories (φ^4 theory, Hubbard model) demonstrating effectiveness in symmetry enforcement and breaking.

problem: Anomaly detection methods for tabular data assume fixed patterns and perform poorly on diverse real-world scenarios; LLMs cannot process heterogeneous data without privacy risks.
approach: Reposition LLM as algorithmist analyzing detector weaknesses to synthesize hard anomalies via Python code, avoiding raw data exposure and enabling data-agnostic synthesis.
contribution: LLM-DAS consistently boosts mainstream AD detector robustness across 36 TAD benchmarks via programmatic synthesis without retraining.

problem: Foundation models' performance on open-ended, multimodal reasoning tasks with undefined problem structure (as in real-world discovery) remains largely untested.
approach: Introduce PuzzleWorld benchmark of 667 puzzlehunt problems with detailed reasoning traces and skill labels to assess step-by-step creative reasoning.
contribution: Best model solves only 14% of puzzles with 40% stepwise accuracy, matching human novices but falling behind enthusiasts; fine-tuning on traces improves stepwise accuracy from 4% to 11%.

problem: The interplay between in-weight learning (permanent parameter updates) and in-context learning (ephemeral activation modulation) in Transformers remains theoretically unclear.
approach: Operationalize evolutionary concepts (environmental stability, cue reliability) in controlled tasks to characterize how conditions influence IWL vs. ICL preference.
contribution: Show stable environments favor IWL with sharp transitions, volatile environments with reliable cues favor ICL, revealing task-dependent learning strategy transitions.

problem: Functional data classification is impeded by phase variability (temporal misalignments) typically handled separately from classification via sequential registration and classification.
approach: Jointly learn diffeomorphic warping and classifier within unified architecture using neural deformation, Fourier spectral representation, and class-aware contrastive loss.
contribution: DeepFRC provides first theoretical guarantees for joint registration-classification, proving optimal warping approximation with generalization bound linking registration fidelity to classification.

problem: Counterintuitive RL results on LLMs (single example matching full dataset, inaccurate rewards sufficient, negative sampling outperforming reward methods) have unclear preconditions.
approach: Systematically examine conditions under which these phenomena hold by identifying model-task alignment (pass@k accuracy) as key differentiator.
contribution: Show these counterintuitive results arise only under strong model-task alignment; standard RL remains effective when alignment is weak.

problem: Existing asynchronous SGD methods struggle under heterogeneous worker computation speeds and non-IID data distributions while lacking optimal theoretical guarantees.
approach: Introduce Ringleader ASGD achieving first-order stochastic method lower bounds for smooth nonconvex optimization without restrictive data similarity assumptions.
contribution: Attain optimal time complexity under arbitrary and time-varying worker computation speeds, closing fundamental gap in asynchronous optimization theory.

problem: RLVR training of multimodal LLMs suffers from entropy collapse and policy degradation due to enormous state space and sparse rewards without proper exploration guidance.
approach: Propose CalibRL hybrid-policy framework with distribution-aware advantage weighting and asymmetric activation to preserve exploration while using expert guidance as calibration.
contribution: Increase policy entropy in guided manner across eight benchmarks with improved balance between exploration and exploitation.

problem: Equivariant universal machine learning interatomic potentials achieve high accuracy but suffer from computational cost due to expensive tensor products and high-degree representations.
approach: Develop MatRIS invariant uMLIP using attention-based three-body interaction modeling with separable attention mechanism achieving O(N) linear complexity.
contribution: MatRIS matches leading equivariant models on benchmarks (Matbench-Discovery F1=0.847) while improving training efficiency by 13.0-13.5× at comparable accuracy.

problem: Distributed training with adaptive optimizers using infrequent communication suffers performance degradation due to time-scale mismatch between optimizer momentum (tuned for frequent updates) and long intervals.
approach: Propose MT-DAO with multiple slow/fast-moving first momenta tracking dynamics across different time scales, with first convergence guarantees.
contribution: Eliminate performance gap with fully synchronous DDP, reduce iso-token wall-clock time by 6-27% on Ethernet and reach target perplexity 24% faster at 720M scale.

problem: General protein language models generalize poorly to specific target proteins not in training data; practitioners need accurate predictions for individual proteins they study.
approach: Enable self-supervised customization of protein LMs to individual target proteins on-the-fly via Protein Test-Time Training (ProteinTTT) without additional data.
contribution: ProteinTTT consistently improves structure/fitness/function prediction across models and datasets; achieves state-of-the-art on protein fitness, improves 19% of Big Fantastic Virus Database.

problem: Multi-source RAG systems aggregate all sources uniformly or statically select single source, ignoring semantic complementarity and document contribution to generation objective.
approach: Perform gradient-aware re-ranking estimating document contribution to loss via single backward pass; incorporate inter-source redundancy for source combination selection.
contribution: GRO-RAG achieves consistent improvements in generation quality on multi-source QA and open-domain tasks with theoretical guarantees on gradient-based Top-k selection.

problem: Diffusion Q-Learning relies on multi-step denoising making both training and inference slow and fragile for offline RL.
approach: Reformulate DQL within Flow Matching paradigm to learn average velocity field supporting one-step action generation, removing need for multi-step denoising.
contribution: One-Step Flow Q-Learning (OFQL) generates actions in single step while substantially reducing computation and outperforming multi-step DQL by large margin on D4RL.

problem: Transformers typically require advanced optimizers like AdamW rather than momentum SGD due to heavy-tailed gradient distributions limiting optimization theory applicability.
approach: Engineer Deeply Normalized Transformer (DNT) with strategic normalization at proper positions to modulate Jacobian matrices, balance weights/activations, and concentrate gradient distributions.
contribution: DNT trains effectively with vanilla momentum SGD while yielding comparable performance to AdamW-trained Transformers, outperforming ViT and GPT counterparts.

problem: Relationship between overparameterization, stability, and generalization for discontinuous classifiers remains incompletely understood.
approach: Establish generalization bound for finite function classes improving inversely with class stability (margin to decision boundary), deriving law of robustness for classification.
contribution: Show interpolating models with p≈n parameters must be unstable, necessitating substantial overparameterization for high stability; stability correlates with test performance.

problem: Reasoning LLMs generate long thinking traces whose utility is unclear; overthinking on easy instances wastes computation tokens.
approach: Analyze entropy patterns across difficulty levels (U-shape: high on simple/hard, low on medium); predict difficulty from hidden states to adaptively allocate Easy/Normal/Hard reasoning strategies.
contribution: DiffAdapt achieves comparable/improved accuracy while reducing token usage by up to 22.4% across five models and eight benchmarks without retraining.

problem: Vision-language models can infer sensitive locations from images at street-level precision without respecting contextual privacy norms and disclosure expectations.
approach: Evaluate whether VLMs respect contextual integrity by interpreting social norms and contextual cues to determine appropriate location disclosure levels.
contribution: VLM-GEOPRIVACY benchmark shows 14 leading VLMs poorly align with human privacy expectations, over-disclosing in sensitive contexts and vulnerable to prompt attacks.

problem: Diffusion transformers employ modulation-based text conditioning via pooled embeddings alongside attention, yet whether modulation provides performance advantage remains unclear.
approach: Analyze whether pooled embeddings contribute to performance; reframe pooled embedding from conditioning to guidance enabling controllable shifts toward desirable properties.
contribution: Show conventional pooled embedding contributes little but becomes significant when used for guidance and controllable generation, training-free with negligible overhead.

problem: Online convex optimization with unknown discount factor lacks methods adapting to unknown λ while maintaining uniform regret across continuous λ interval.
approach: Maintain multiple OGD instances for different discount factors aggregated by Discounted-Normal-Predictor, analyzing how DNP combines expert decisions with different discount factors.
contribution: Smoothed OGD achieves uniform O(√(log T/(1-λ))) discounted regret for all λ in continuous interval simultaneously.

problem: Pretrained diffusion models trained on Gaussian-corrupted images face distribution gap when processing low-resolution inputs, hindering direct inference for super-resolution.
approach: Train image encoder mapping LR inputs into latent distribution aligned with diffusion model's training space; adaptively predict noise level based on input degradation.
contribution: DM-SR achieves superior perceptual quality with single-stage diffusion without modifying pretrained model, setting new direction for efficient high-fidelity super-resolution.
